Overview of REPHY data

We investigate the REPHY database. See user manual.

Todo

Setup

Code 
library(renv)
renv::load()
library(targets)
library(here)
tar_config_set(
  store = here::here("_targets")
)
library(ggplot2)
library(hrbrthemes)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
devtools::load_all()
riversea::nice_theme()

We begin by reading the .csv file, which is not an easy step because of the formatting issue. One it’s done we can have a look at the data structure.

Here are the parameters that are relevant for our study.

Code 
raw_data |>
  select("Résultat : Code paramètre", "Résultat : Libellé paramètre") |>
  distinct() |>
  filter(`Résultat : Code paramètre` %in% rephy_nutrient_codes())
# A tibble: 4 × 2
  `Résultat : Code paramètre` `Résultat : Libellé paramètre`
  <chr>                       <chr>                         
1 NH4                         Ammonium                      
2 OXYGENE                     Oxygène dissous               
3 PO4                         Phosphate                     
4 NO3+NO2                     Nitrate + nitrite

Next, we clean the table. Rename and select the relevant columns. Filter for the parameters above.

data <- tar_read(rephy_data)

Data completeness

For each nutrient parameter, here is the number of observations, the number of distinct sampling sites, and the covered date range.

Code 
riversea::summarise_rephy_coverage(data) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
parameter_code n n_sites year_min year_max
NH4 19774 153 1989 2022
NO3+NO2 18879 150 2001 2022
OXYGENE 44782 235 1988 2022
PO4 19733 151 1992 2022

We notice that we have more than twice as many points for the oxygen than for the nutrients. The number of points for the other nutrients are closed to one another, suggesting that when one nutrient is measured the others are too.

Spatial coverage

We map the distinct sampling sites to get a sense of the spatial resolution of the REPHY network.

Code 
riversea::plot_rephy_map(data, facet = FALSE)

Grouping by parameter shows that spatial coverage is fairly consistent across the four nutrients: sites are not more likely to be missing one nutrient than another.

Code 
riversea::plot_rephy_map(data, facet = TRUE)

Interstingly we see that concentration of nitrogen derivatives, ammonium and nitrite + nitrate, are higher on Britany coast. This could be expected because of agricultural nutrient runoff.

Temporal coverage

Here is the number of observations per parameter, by year.

Code 
riversea::plot_rephy_temporal_coverage(data)

Nitrate + nitrite (NO3+NO2) is only reported from 1998 onwards, and sampling effort increases markedly from 2009 for all parameters. We should keep this in mind when comparing periods.

Temporal trends by district

To plot a yearly time series per nutrient we need a geographic grouping. We reuse the DCE hydrographic districts already used for the river food web (hydrographic_area, built from the SANDRE coastal/transitional water body shapefiles), so that river and coastal analyses stay on the same spatial units. Each site is joined to the district it falls in, dropping the few sites too far from any polygon to be matched reliably.

Code 
district_data <- tar_read(rephy_district_data)

sites <- data |>
  distinct(site_id, longitude, latitude) |>
  mutate(matched = site_id %in% district_data$site_id)

hydro_area <- tar_read(hydrographic_area) |>
  filter(district %in% unique(district_data$district))
Code 
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = hydro_area, aes(fill = district),  alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = sites, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = matched)) +
  coord_sf(xlim = range(sites$longitude), ylim = range(sites$latitude)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey20", `FALSE` = "red")) +
  labs(fill = "District", color = "Matched", x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  theme(legend.box = "vertical")

507 points out of 103168 could not be matched to a district and were dropped. We then average nutrient concentrations by year and district.

Code 
yearly <- tar_read(rephy_yearly)
str(yearly)
tibble [322 × 5] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)
 $ year          : num [1:322] 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 ...
 $ district      : chr [1:322] "Ardour-Garonne" "Ardour-Garonne" "Ardour-Garonne" "Ardour-Garonne" ...
 $ parameter_code: chr [1:322] "NH4" "NH4" "NH4" "NH4" ...
 $ value         : num [1:322] 2.07 2.39 2.52 1.58 1.76 ...
 $ n             : int [1:322] 24 54 62 160 142 144 151 165 163 223 ...
Code 
riversea::plot_rephy_temporal_trend(yearly |> filter(year >= 2000))

The Loire district stands out with clearly higher nitrate + nitrite and phosphate concentrations, consistent with agricultural nutrient runoff from the Loire basin. We filter early years because we have very few observations.
